title: Attributable executions and revision-aware target availability
summary: Separate execution/verification from delivered code. Expose current target evidence without blocking unrelated planning.
description:
Integration context: every agent uses planner load against one shared service; preserve independent session/context/execution attribution, including requester and executor as audit (planner writes are not restricted between agents). Only explicitly enrolled room agents bind to Heca. Native transcript aggregation is outside this delivery.

Purpose: Separate execution/verification from delivered code. Expose current target evidence without blocking unrelated planning.

Current state: this phase is planned; current production persistence remains JSON until the SQLite/API migration is implemented. Reuse existing capabilities instead of creating another planner.

- P129(F025)/T492: Per-target integration history and honest present code availability.

Execution contract:
Follow the task dependencies and the phase priority in the rebuilt F025 plan. Keep coherent phase work and recover approved detours; do not introduce a global task queue or silently preempt active work. Use the user-scoped service/SQLite boundary, explicit workspace identity, complete bounded context and revision-bound evidence wherever applicable.

Acceptance:
Each task proves its stated outcome; preserve IDs/history, single-owner decisions and phase handoffs. Mechanical parent/dependency effects are consistent; semantic review is factual, reviewed-unchanged or explicitly pending. Native/provider/installed claims need their actual owner evidence.

tasks.title: Persist attributable task executions and revision-bound verification
tasks.description:
Attribution contract: Implement independent standalone/integrated execution history using agentId, planner sessionId, nativeSessionId when known, harness/model/source identity, requestedBySessionId versus executionSessionId (audit only; planner writes are not restricted between agents), policy revision and lifecycle observations. Resolve parents server-side; retain name/role/model snapshots. Native IDs are correlation, never credentials or owner overrides. A disconnected agent does not imply finished work.

Outcome: Attributable task executions and exact-revision verification records independent of target delivery.

Current implementation: Tasks have a lifecycle/owner and pause history, but no durable attempt model separating results from different workspaces and code revisions.

Implementation responsibility:
- Add execution identity/lifecycle and granular operations linking task, authenticated caller, stable workspace, baseline/configuration and attributable result commits or recoverable dirty snapshots.
- Define running/paused/verified/failed/abandoned transitions and same-attempt resume checks without overwriting earlier attempts.
- Bind tests/conformity to command/suite, environment, source/configuration fingerprint and coverage limits; later edits invalidate current verification without deleting history.
- Provide the identity/checkpoint port T471 changesets and phase handoffs consume. Preserve foreign dirty changes and unknown historical attribution.
- Handle non-code work without fabricated commits/PRs. AgentTest remains an evidence producer seam, not an approved autonomous testing platform.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Two attempts retain one task ID and separately attributable evidence.
- Verified uncommitted code has recoverable evidence but is not reported as integrated.
- Native session, planner caller and execution IDs cannot be conflated or client-set to steal work.

tasks.title: Track target integrations and revalidate current code availability
tasks.description:
Outcome: Per-target integration history and honest present code availability.

Current implementation: A task marked done does not establish that its code exists in main/develop/another worktree. Squash/rebase/cherry-pick and reverts complicate simple SHA ancestry.

Implementation responsibility:
- Record configurable target integrations against attributable execution artifacts, target revision and provenance without triggering automatic Git actions.
- Distinguish historical merge from current availability, and expose present/absent/unknown/review-required evidence.
- Handle normal merge, squash/rebase/cherry-pick, target replacement and revert with bounded evidence; never claim general semantic equivalence from a hash match.
- Revalidate affected source-dependent verification at the selected source/configuration. Retain legacy unknowns and non-code task projections.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Merging dev-a/feat-one does not mark dev-b/feat-two delivered.
- A later revert preserves historical integration while invalidating current availability.
- Deleting/renaming a worktree/branch does not erase execution evidence.

tasks.title: Expose work progress and target availability in planner context and UI
tasks.description:
Outcome: Separate global work progress, workspace evidence and target-delivery views.

Current implementation: Current task/parent statuses are a single operational projection. The selector must consume availability only when work actually needs produced source.

Implementation responsibility:
- Expose execution/verification/source/target counters and explanations through read models and UI, preserving derived parent work status.
- Integrate the T463 availability extension without changing global priority or turning all work dependencies into code-delivery dependencies.
- Scope context and evidence to selected workspace/target revision; navigation must not silently redirect active writes.
- Mark stale/unknown/reverted evidence and retain non-code/legacy compatibility without fabricated results.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Global verified progress and target availability can differ visibly and correctly.
- A source-dependent successor is not told to use unavailable code; unrelated planning work is not blocked on a merge.
- Current target selection and evidence provenance remain visible in agent and supervisor results.
